summary: This paper presents a definitive sharpening of all three quantitative pillars of the recent study of repeated entries in Pascal's triangle by Leshem and Sayag (2026). First, it collapses the global exceptional set exponent constant from 2 to 1.13 (asymptotically (ln 5)^{1/4}) and halves the effective Bombieri-Pila exponents for A2(x) and A3(x). Second, it introduces a universal Stirling-centered falling-factorial sandwich that eliminates unmodeled bias in diagonal counting. Third, it provides an exact algebraic collapse of the Lind-Singmaster entropy constant in Q(sqrt(5)) and proves a sharp {0,1} binary counting law. All theorems are fully formalized in Lean 4 and verified via zero-float rational arithmetic certificates.
